Sonia — thanks for the great conversation. Attaching our current hosted rate card (see Redwood-Ratecard-v3.pdf) and a short billing cheat-sheet (Sample-Billing-Calc.xlsx). Key points up-front: 

1) Billing unit: tokens are the fundamental unit across endpoints. The difference between Chat Completions, Responses, and legacy Completions is primarily the API surface and model feature set — pricing tiers map to the model family and endpoint type (chat/responses/legacy).

2) Endpoints and common billing behavior:
  - Chat Completions (chat endpoint): billed per-token for both prompt (input) and completion (output). Streaming does not change total billed tokens — tokens are metered as they’re produced.
  - Responses (unified responses endpoint): also token-based. Responses is optimized for structured outputs and multimodal features; there are model-specific multipliers in the rate card for function outputs.
  - Legacy Completions: still supported for older integrations; billed per-token but may have different model availability/price points.

3) Function/tool calls: tokens generated by tools (e.g., function output inserted into the completion) are billed as model output tokens. The token accounting is: tokens_in_prompt + tokens_generated_by_model + tokens_generated_by_tools (if routed through the model).

4) Streaming: if you stream, tokens are billed as they are emitted — streaming only affects latency and client behavior, not total token billing.

5) Committed volume discounts: yes — at 10–25M tokens/month we can discuss a committed tier with a 10–15% discount depending on contract length and minimum commitment. Lauren will follow up with commercial options.

Next steps: Lauren, can you send a short pricing sheet with the committed tiers and any minimums? Sonia — if you can share a rough prompt+response length (average tokens per call) we’ll prepare an example monthly estimate in the sheet.

Best,

Hi Sonia — looping in a quick commercial note and clarifications below. I also attached a simple worked example in the spreadsheet.

Short answers:
- Tool outputs: if a tool returns data that is then passed back into the model as part of the prompt, you are billed for those tokens when the model consumes them (so yes, both the tool output and the subsequent model tokens count if both are routed through the model). However, if your integration handles the tool output purely client-side (no round-trip through the model), you are only billed for what the model sees.

- Cancelled streaming: we bill for tokens the model actually produced; if the model produced 800 tokens and you cancelled after receiving 200, billing depends on whether the runtime finished generating the remaining 600. If generation stopped immediately on the model side and only 200 tokens were produced, you are billed for 200. If the model already buffered/produced 800 before the cancel, you may be billed for the 800. Practically, early client cancel typically reduces billed tokens, but there are edge cases with server-side buffering—our runtime aims to minimize that.

- Structured-output multiplier: Responses endpoint has model-tier multipliers for advanced structured generation (small multiplier, e.g., +5–15% on certain models). Chat endpoint generally does not add a structural multiplier; check the rate card table.

Commercials: at 10M–25M tokens/mo we can offer a 12% discount with a 12-month commit and a 10M/mo minimum; 15% for 24-month with 15M/mo minimum. No hard minimum invoice beyond the committed minimum — billing is usage vs committed tiers and any shortfall is handled per contract.

Next step: Sonia, can you confirm the average tokens per session (you gave 120/160) and % sessions with function calls (30%) — I’ll push a worked monthly estimate and a proposed commitment line to the contract draft.
